description: CI regenerates the CRDs and dist/ that a version bump implies, and pushes them back onto the Renovate branch as github-actions[bot] (see .github/workflows/ci.yaml). gitIgnoredAuthors keeps Renovate from treating that commit as a third-party modification, which would otherwise block both rebasing and automerge. Automerge is platform-native (the default): the `main` ruleset requires the CI check, which is both what makes auto-merge armable at all and what holds the merge until the regenerated head commit is green.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security remediation, kept separate from the ordinary update flow: ungrouped so a fix is never held behind an unrelated bump in the same branch, and labelled so it is obvious in the PR list. This was previously dead - a packageRule with `enabled: false` suppresses vulnerability PRs for that manager too, so the blanket npm/bun disable meant no advisory for cdk8s, constructs or any transitive dep ever produced one. Requires Dependabot alerts to be enabled on the repo; Renovate reads them, it does not run its own scanner.

packageRules.description: package.json/bun.lock bumps get PRs, but never automerge by default. This used to be a blanket `enabled: false` justified by CLAUDE.md's 'confirm before adding dependencies' policy, but that policy governs *adding* a dependency, not bumping one already in the tree - and conflating the two meant nothing was watching. The manual path (`mise run upgrade`) went unexercised long enough for cdk8s-plus-34 to sit 13 patch releases behind inside its own caret range. The safety net here is unusually good: CI synthesizes every manifest, so the dist/ diff on the PR *is* the blast radius, rendered. Read that diff and merge. Must name `bun`, not just `npm`: because bun.lock exists, the bun manager claims package.json and the npm manager never sees it, so matching npm alone silently matches nothing.

Nothing in devDependencies can change a rendered manifest on the PR that bumps it - these only format, lint, type-check, or generate the values-schema types. If a bump breaks, CI goes red and nothing reaches the cluster, so there is no dist/ diff worth a human's time. Grouped into one PR and automerged on green. One caveat, deliberately accepted: cdk8s-cli does generate checked-in code (imports/), but only via `mise run imports`, which is manual and needs live cluster access - it is not in the build or pre-commit chain, so an automerged bump cannot rewrite imports/ by itself; it just means the next time someone runs that task by hand they get a newer generator, and they review that diff then. Minor/patch only: a major here (typescript 7, oxlint 2) is a rule/behaviour change worth reading, and an oxfmt major can reformat every .ts file in the repo - CI would push the reformat back onto the branch and it would still be correct, but that is a diff someone should see.

cdk8s-plus is versioned per Kubernetes minor - the `-34` suffix is k8s 1.34 - so it belongs to the same 'tracks the cluster' category as the kubectl pin, not to its own release cadence. There is no cdk8s-plus-35 published yet, so this is a future move rather than a present gap, but when one lands it is a package rename plus a construct-API sweep across every app, and it must land deliberately alongside a k3s upgrade. Kept ungrouped so it can never ride in on someone else's branch, and explicit here rather than relying on the blanket rule above so that removing that rule cannot silently arm this one.

Chart/CRD version bumps (the custom.regex managers below) are fully self-completing once CI pushes the regenerated CRDs + dist/, and CI synthesizes and validates the exact manifests Argo will apply. Let minor/patch automerge on green; majors still get regenerated onto the branch by CI, but wait for a human to actually look at the CRD diff before Argo applies it.

The argo-cd chart controls ArgoCD itself, and this cluster runs ArgoCD in manual-sync mode on purpose -- an automerged bump lands on main and Argo notices the new manifest, which fires a sync alert for a change nobody asked to deploy yet. Keep the bump controllable end-to-end by a human: Renovate opens the PR and CI regenerates dist/, but the merge (and therefore the deploy trigger) waits for the same person who is going to actually sync it. Sits below the custom.regex automerge rule so it wins on conflict, matching how the vectorchord and k3s entries opt out of that same blanket.

k3s cluster upgrades roll every node and change the Kubernetes API surface. Renovate can open the PR and push the regenerated dist/, but a human must schedule the outage and read the release notes before Argo applies it -- never automerge.

The vectorchord ImageCatalog entry in apps/postgres/app.ts is a Postgres image for a live database, and the repository publishes every major side by side (18.3-1.1.0 sits next to 17.10-1.1.1). Cap the entry to its own major line: without this Renovate reads the tag as an ordinary version and offers 18.x for the major-17 entry, which CNPG would treat as an in-place major upgrade rather than an image bump. Also require the `-<vchord-version>` suffix: the registry publishes an unsuffixed alias per pg patch (e.g. `17.10`) that floats and gets silently repointed across vchord releases, and under `loose` versioning that bare tag sorts as a newer "release" than the suffixed one it's an alias of, so Renovate offers it as a patch bump (#42/#43). Pinning to the suffixed form keeps every bump an explicit, reproducible tag change.

Opt the Postgres images back out of the blanket custom.regex automerge above. A chart bump that breaks renders red in CI; a bad Postgres image passes CI and then rolls a database. These get read by a human.

The velero CLI renders its own CRDs, so mise.toml's pin and tools/sources.ts' pin must match -- sources.ts hard-fails the render otherwise. Renovate sees them through two managers (mise, custom.regex) under two depNames, which would mean two PRs that each fail CI alone and can only go green once both land. Group them so they always move as one. Deliberately not scoped to minor/patch: a major has to stay grouped too.
Mirror of the custom.regex automerge rule above, for the mise-managed half of the grouped velero PR -- a grouped branch only automerges if every dependency in it is allowed to.

cdk8s shells out to `helm template`, and its integration is built against Helm 3 -- Helm 4 is a different CLI contract, so an automatic major would break every HelmApp render at once. Minor/patch within 3.x is fine and still flows through normally.

Images this repo pins to a release *line* rather than to a version. Each has an argocd-image-updater entry that moves it within that line, so the pin is a ceiling, not a version -- and nothing was watching the ceiling. authentik sat at 2026.8.x while a calendar-versioned product shipped a minor a month; resilio-sync's `digest` strategy on a fixed 2.8.1 tag is a total freeze that reads like a pin; and netbox/immich/mealie/atuin/bookorbit/valkey/gotenberg would each go a major behind in silence. These get a PR and a `pinned` label, never an automerge: every one of them is a migration, a schema change, or (external-dns) a line whose minors have already deleted live DNS records once. Listed by depName rather than by manager so it survives a pin moving between files.

Don't restate what argocd-image-updater already does. For the entries above whose constraint is a major line (`v4.x.x`, `8-alpine`, `v3`), the updater takes every minor and patch within it on its own, and a Renovate PR for the same bump is pure noise against a base the updater does not even read -- it writes .argocd-source-<app>.yaml, not the manifest. Leaving these enabled would also let them ride the blanket custom.regex automerge above. Only the major, which the constraint deliberately blocks, is worth a human's attention.

Same idea, one notch finer: authentik and external-dns are capped at a *minor* line, not a major one, so the patch is what the updater already handles and the minor is the one nobody would otherwise hear about. resilio-sync is deliberately absent from both suppression rules -- its constraint reaches nothing at all, so every update type is news.

Hand-rolled sidecars with no argocd-image-updater entry at all, so Renovate is the only thing that will ever mention a new version. blackbox-exporter was `:latest` with `imagePullPolicy: Always`, which meant the running version changed on any pod restart and git recorded none of it. The two Postgres client images are pinned to the major of the servers they talk to (both clusters are 17), and python is the energy collector's runtime -- none of these should land unread on green, so no automerge; `postgres` and `python` are scoped to the docker datasource because the bare names are also plausible npm packages.

kubectl is only supported within one minor of the apiserver, so this pin belongs to the cluster's k3s release, not to kubectl's own release cadence -- left to float it drifts ahead of the cluster and silently changes KUBE_VERSION, which feeds `helm template`'s .Capabilities and re-renders manifests. It moves by hand alongside K3S_VERSION in lib/consts.ts, in the same PR as the k3s bump that a human already has to review.

k3s.description: k3s channel server: tracks the 'stable' channel so Renovate proposes the same release the upstream installer would recommend, rather than the newest GitHub tag.

customManagers.description: Bump literal versions pinned in tools/sources.ts (velero, kured, sealed-secrets, system-upgrade-controller, and the still-disabled cnpg entries awaiting that app's migration out of the legacy prod repo), each annotated with a `// renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment directly above the `value` field.

Bump chart/release versions pinned in any apps/*/*.ts or lib/*.ts, annotated the same way as the literal versions in tools/sources.ts. Two shapes are matched: a top-level `const <name> = "..."` (the common case, and what tools/sources.ts reads back via VersionSource kind 'app-const'), and an inline `version: "..."` inside a HelmApp call for the charts that never needed a named const. `registryUrl` is optional and only carried by the `datasource=helm` entries -- the helm datasource has no default registry to fall back on, so a chart without it resolves to nothing and is silently skipped. lib/ is in scope because the shared constructs pin images too (mariadb in lib/mysql.ts, exportarr in lib/media-app.ts, valkey in lib/valkey.ts, the cluster's k3s release in lib/consts.ts), and those went untracked for as long as the pattern only listed apps/. Every .ts under an app is in scope, not just app.ts: blackbox-exporter (apps/metrics/blackbox.ts) and the pg-dump image (apps/postgres/pg-dump.ts) both sat completely unwatched behind the narrower pattern, since an app's helper modules are exactly where hand-rolled sidecars end up.
